> **WIP: not yet human-reviewed.** AI assistance (Claude 5.5 + GPT 6.1 Sol) was used to write this PR.
> **TODO:** human review of the tests, benchmarks, diff and maintainability before this is marked ready.

ModelOpt block checkpoints such as `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB` (IQ2_XXS experts, Q8_0 dense layers) only run on SM120/SM121, because b12x is their only kernel path. On every other GPU, loading fails with `Block-quantized dense weights require b12x on SM12x`. This PR adds a Triton path for NVIDIA SM75+. SM120/SM121 keep b12x by default.

Fixes #62609 

**Not a duplicate:** #59486  is the b12x support for SM120/SM121 that this PR falls back from, and no open PR adds a path for other GPUs. I claimed the work in #62609 on 2026-10-22.

**Related:** Bolt in FP16 also needs a separate NemotronH bugfix PR (link TBD). Without it, FP16 Bolt scores 3/250 on GSM8K with any backend. See Details.

## Claims

- Bolt loads and serves on SM80, SM86, SM89 and SM90. The weights stay packed at 21.7 GiB.
- BF16 GSM8K-250 scores 230–236 across four GPUs (run-to-run spread is about ±5).
- The kernels support FP16 activations:
  - Kernel tests pass in FP16 on every tested GPU.
  - Full-model FP16 GSM8K scores 234–235 with the separate FP16 fix, at BF16 speed.
- On Turing (SM75), FMA tiles are used instead of tensor-core `tl.dot`. They cross-compile without spills (checked with ptxas), but have not been run on Turing hardware.
- Nothing compiles during inference: a warmup compiles every reachable kernel config before CUDA graph capture.
- Default behavior on SM120/SM121 is unchanged: b12x is still selected there.

## Validation

### GPUs and tests

| GPU | SM | Memory | `test_modelopt_block_triton.py` | `test_modelopt.py -k block` | Full model |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H200 NVL | 90 | HBM3e | Run on an earlier revision (see TODO) | Earlier revision | BF16 GSM8K + serving |
| A100-class (CMP 170HX, 74 SMs) | 80 | HBM, 63 GiB | 192 passed, 2 min 51 s | 55 passed | BF16 + FP16 GSM8K, serving |
| L40S | 89 | GDDR6, 44 GiB | 192 passed, 3 min 9 s | 55 passed | BF16 + FP16 GSM8K, serving |
| RTX 3090 | 86 | GDDR6X, 24 GiB | 192 passed, 2 min 4 s | 55 passed | BF16 GSM8K (eager) |
| RTX 5060 Ti | 120 | GDDR7, 16 GiB | 191 passed, 1 skipped (needs 12 GiB free) | 55 passed | — (16 GiB) |
| T4 | 75 | — | not run | not run | — |

**Commands:**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_modelopt_block_triton.py
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k block
```

**What the tests check:**
- The kernel tests compare against an exact ggml reference decode. `dequantize_blocks` is also bit-exact on every tensor of the real Bolt checkpoint.
- The block tests serve a tiny Nemotron-H end to end in BF16 and FP16.
- The warmup check reported no inference-time JIT from these kernels in BF16 or FP16. The only kernel that compiled at inference was upstream Mamba's `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`.

### GSM8K-250

**Setup:**
- The first 250 test questions, sent to `/v1/completions` with the prompt `Q: {question}\nA: Let's think step by step.\n`.
- Temperature 0, `max_tokens` 768, 32 requests at a time.
- The prediction is the last number in the output. 225 is the pass bar.
- BF16 varies between 230 and 235 on identical code.

| GPU | BF16 | FP16 with the FP16 fix | FP16 without it |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H200 NVL | 236 | — | — |
| A100-class | 230, 231 | 235 | 3 |
| L40S | 235, 230, 232 | 234 | 3 |
| RTX 3090 | 231 | — | — |

### Serving, BF16

**Setup:** `vllm bench serve` with random data, 128 tokens in and 256 out, `--ignore-eos`, temperature 0. Each run used 12 prompts at c=1 and 32 prompts otherwise. Cells show output tok/s, with median TPOT in parentheses.

| GPU | c=1 | c=8 | c=16 | c=32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H200 NVL ¹ | 132.1 (7.1 ms) | 492.0 (15.1 ms) | — | 865.0 (34.1 ms) |
| A100-class | 80.3 (11.7 ms) | 218.6 (34.2 ms) | 311.4 (48.1 ms) | 402.6 (73.3 ms) |
| L40S ² | 87.5 (10.6 ms) | 346.9 (21.0 ms) | 486, 512 | 623, 615 |

**Footnotes:**
1. The H200 run used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.55` with `modelopt_iq2_dense_cache` on.
2. L40S c=16 and c=32 are two runs each with this PR's MoE setting (GEMV up to 8 rows). c=1 and c=8 come from the run just before that change, where those batch sizes already took the same path.

**FP16 vs BF16 speed** (A100-class, with the FP16 fix), c=1/8/32:

| Dtype | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 81.1 | 219.4 | 395.0 |
| BF16 | 80.3 | 218.6 | 402.6 |

There is no "before" column, because the model does not load on these GPUs without this PR.

**Commands:**

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32]}' \
  --kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant":{"nvfp4_w4a16":"marlin"}}'

vllm bench serve --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256 \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 32 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0

python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_modelopt_block_triton.py
```

The NVFP4 Mamba projections were pinned to Marlin so every GPU used the same backend. The auto choice also works: it picked Humming on the H200 and served at the same speed.

<details>
<summary>Which revision each run used</summary>

Development history, unsquashed: `blazingbhavneek/vllm`, branch `feature/modelopt-block-triton`.

- **5060 Ti:** ran this exact commit.
- **A100-class:** ran `ff9dd45e8b`, which also contains the FP16 fix. HBM dispatch is identical to this PR.
- **L40S:**
  - Tests and GSM8K ran at `ff9dd45e8b` and `34fa2bdf52`.
  - The c=16/32 serving runs used `34fa2bdf52`.
- **RTX 3090:** ran `34fa2bdf52`.
- **Changes after `34fa2bdf52`:**
  - The GDDR IQ2_XXS dense cutoff moved from 128 to 65. A microbenchmark on the 5060 Ti, 3090 and L40S shows dequant 1.4–2.1x faster at M=96. This only affects M = 65–127.
  - A comment-only cleanup that also removes an always-on constexpr flag.
- **H200:** the round before the SM90 single-row Q8 GEMV was added (see TODO).

</details>

## Details

### Design

**Dispatch inside custom ops.** The choice that depends on M (rows, i.e. tokens in the batch) happens inside custom ops (`modelopt_block_linear` and the MoE experts), so torch.compile cannot freeze it. The IQ2 grid lookup table is built at load time, so CUDA graphs capture.

**Dense layers:**
- A GEMV for small M.
- A fused-decode `tl.dot` GEMM with deterministic split-K.
- From a per-codec M onward, dequantize then cuBLAS, as AWQ does. The dequantized copy is capped at 2^26 elements.

| Path | HBM | GDDR | Turing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| IQ2_XXS dense: dequant + cuBLAS from M = | 8 | 65 | 32 (roofline estimate) |
| Q8_0 dense: dequant + cuBLAS from M = | 64 | 256 | 32 (roofline estimate) |
| MoE GEMV up to M = | 8 | 8 | 8 |

- **Memory class:** a GPU counts as HBM when its memory bus is at least 1024 bits wide. The dequantized copy is a write plus a read of 2 bytes per weight, so the crossover follows memory bandwidth.
- **Why 65 for IQ2 on GDDR:** past one 64-row M tile the fused IQ2 GEMM doubles in cost. On the 5060 Ti it goes from 213 to 425 µs at M=65, against 254 µs for dequant.

**MoE:**
- A `TritonExperts` subclass. Up to 8 routed rows, one program per row: direct routing without `moe_align_block_size`, with ReLU² fused into the first GEMM using the same BF16 rounding as the unfused path. Above 8 rows, a fused-decode grouped GEMM.
- The cutoff of 8 came from serving, not microbenchmarks. On the A100-class GPU and the L40S, a kernel sweep with uniform routing keeps the GEMV ahead up to M=128, but serving disagrees:
  - On the A100-class GPU, a cutoff of 64 made median TPOT 15% worse at c=16 and 27% worse at c=32.
  - On the L40S, a cutoff of 8 gave 4–12% more tok/s at c=16/32.

**Other parts:**
- Q8_0 embedding lookup.
- On Hopper, single-row Q8_0 on four exact Bolt projection shapes uses one wider-K GEMV kernel.
- An opt-in BF16 cache for IQ2_XXS dense weights (`--kernel-config '{"modelopt_iq2_dense_cache": true}'`, off by default; about 3.28 GiB for Bolt).
- The kernels follow the activation dtype (BF16 or FP16). b12x is BF16-only, so `--dtype half` uses Triton on every GPU.
- Docs: new section "Other NVIDIA GPUs (Triton kernels)" in `docs/features/quantization/b12x.md`.

### Complexity

About 1,340 non-test lines under `vllm/`:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| Kernels (`modelopt_block_quant_triton.py`) | 862, of which 68 are the IQ2 grid table |
| Warmup | 239 |
| MoE experts class | 107 |
| `modelopt_block_quant.py` | +125/−28 (backend selection and wiring) |
| Config | +6 |
| Warmup hook | +4 |

**Why it's worth it:**
- It makes an NVIDIA checkpoint family usable on every NVIDIA GPU that is not SM12x.
- Almost all of it lives in new files. The only existing code it changes is backend selection in `modelopt_block_quant.py` and one warmup hook.
- The alternative is to dequantize to BF16 at load. That needs about 148 GB for Bolt's 74B parameters, against 21.7 GiB packed.

### FP16 dependency, fixed in a separate PR

- `MoERunner._maybe_apply_routed_scale_to_output` divides the shared-expert output by `routed_scaling_factor` (5 for Bolt) in FP16 and expects the model to compensate.
- `nemotron_h` does not compensate, so FP16 Bolt collapses to 3/250 on any backend.
- The fix and its regression test are kept out of this PR.

### Limitations and TODO

- [ ] **Human review:** tests, benchmarks, diff and maintainability.
- [ ] **H200 rerun at this commit:** the SM90 single-row Q8 GEMV was added after the last H200 serving and GSM8K run. If it doesn't hold up, drop that dispatch.
- [ ] **SM75 hardware run** (T4). Otherwise, narrow the claim to SM80+.
- [ ] **GPU sync check:** run `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on the affected configuration.
- **Q8 cutoff on large-L2 GDDR GPUs** (L40S: 96 MiB L2, 142 SMs). Classifying by bus width keeps them on the GDDR value, which is up to 1.44x off the best path at M=128 (`fc2_latent`). This is a follow-up.
- **`lm_head` never dequantizes:** at 2^29 elements it is above the 2^26 cap. It runs 1.6–3.3x slower than BF16 once 64–128 or more sequences are batched. Slicing the dequant would fix this; follow-up.
- **MoE prefill:** the packed grouped GEMM takes 2.3–2.8x as long as BF16 MoE on dequantized weights from M=16 up. That is the cost of keeping weights packed.
- **Out of scope:** IQ2_XS still requires b12x. ROCm is not supported. Routed experts support tensor parallelism only, as with b12x.
- **CI:**
  - The kernel tests run in the existing L4 quantization kernel shards. They take 2–4.5 minutes on the tested GPUs, against a 30-minute timeout.
  - A new L4 step runs the dense-cache and backend-selection tests in `test_modelopt.py`. It removes that file from the test-tethering allowlist.
  - The full model does not fit CI's L4 (24 GB), so it is not exercised in CI. Full-model validation was done outside CI, as above.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""ModelOpt IQ2_XXS / Q8_0 Triton kernels on NVIDIA Nemotron Bolt shapes (TP=1).
+
+Dense layers are compared with bf16 cuBLAS on the dequantized weights, MoE
+layers with vLLM's bf16 Triton `fused_experts`. Timing: CUPTI, CUDA graph,
+cold L2, median.
+
+    python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_modelopt_block_triton.py
+    python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_modelopt_block_triton.py \
+        --layer shared_up --m 1 --sweep
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import statistics
+from functools import partial
+
+import torch
+from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
+
+import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.modelopt_block_triton_moe as moe
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import modular_kernel as mk
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
+    FusedMoEConfig,
+    FusedMoEParallelConfig,
+    FusedMoEQuantConfig,
+    FusedMoEQuantDesc,
+    RoutingMethodType,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe import fused_experts
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize import (
+    MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import modelopt_block_quant_triton as t
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager
+
+DENSE = [
+    ("qkv_proj", "q8_0", 4608, 4096),
+    ("o_proj", "q8_0", 4096, 4096),
+    ("fc1_latent", "q8_0", 1024, 4096),
+    ("fc2_latent", "q8_0", 4096, 1024),
+    ("shared_up", "iq2_xxs", 5376, 4096),
+    ("shared_down", "iq2_xxs", 4096, 5376),
+    ("lm_head", "q8_0", 131072, 4096),
+]
+DENSE_M = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]
+MOE = [("moe_240x2048", 240, 2048), ("moe_432x2560", 432, 2560)]
+MOE += [("moe_496x2560", 496, 2560)]
+MOE_M = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096]
+BLOCK = {"iq2_xxs": (256, 66), "q8_0": (32, 34)}
+
+
+def bench_us(fn):
+    for _ in range(25):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True)) * 1e3
+
+
+def random_blocks(lead, k, codec):
+    size, nbytes = BLOCK[codec]
+    raw = torch.randint(0, 256, (*lead, k // size, nbytes), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    scales = (torch.randn(*lead, k // size) * 2e-3).half()
+    raw[..., :2] = scales.unsqueeze(-1).view(torch.uint8)
+    return t.repack_blocks(raw, codec)
+
+
+def try_time(fn, ref):
+    try:
+        out = fn()
+    except triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources:
+        return None
+    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max() / ref.float().abs().max()
+    assert err < 2e-2, f"wrong result, relative error {err:.3g}"
+    return bench_us(fn)
+
+
+def linear_sweep(M, K):
+    # Odd splits too: shared_down has 5376 = 21 * 256 steps, so only 3 and 7 fit.
+    for bn, bk, split, warps, stages in itertools.product(
+        (8, 16, 32, 64, 128),
+        (64, 128, 256),
+        (1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16),
+        (1, 2, 4, 8),
+        (1, 2, 3),
+    ):
+        if K % (split * bk):
+            continue
+        gemv = (triton.next_power_of_2(M),) if M <= 8 else ()
+        gemm = (16, 32, 64, 128) if M > 1 and bn >= 16 else ()
+        for bm in gemv + gemm:
+            yield {"BM": bm, "BN": bn, "BK": bk, "SPLIT": split}, warps, stages
+
+
+def bench_dense(args, props, rows):
+    for name, codec, N, K in DENSE:
+        if args.layer not in (None, name):
+            continue
+        qweight, scales = random_blocks((N,), K, codec)
+        lut = t.iq2_lut(qweight.device) if codec == "iq2_xxs" else None
+        w = t.dequantize_blocks(qweight, scales, lut, codec)
+        bpw = BLOCK[codec][1] / BLOCK[codec][0]
+        for M in args.m or DENSE_M:
+            if name == "lm_head" and M > 512:
+                continue
+            x = torch.randn(M, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            ref = x @ w.T
+            dequant = t.dequant_min_m(codec, torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+            if dequant <= M and N * K <= t.DEQUANT_MAX_NUMEL:
+                cfg = "dequant+cuBLAS"
+            else:
+                cfg = t._linear_config(
+                    M, N, K, codec, props.multi_processor_count,
+                    props.shared_memory_per_block_optin, props.major,
+                )  # fmt: skip
+            run = partial(t._modelopt_block_linear, x, qweight, scales, lut, codec)
+            timed = [(try_time(run, ref), cfg)]
+            for c, wp, st in linear_sweep(M, K) if args.sweep else ():
+                c = {**c, "num_warps": wp, "num_stages": st}
+                run = partial(t.launch_linear, x, qweight, scales, lut, codec, c)
+                if (us := try_time(run, ref)) is not None:
+                    timed.append((us, c))
+            us, cfg = min(timed, key=lambda r: r[0])
+            cublas = bench_us(partial(torch.matmul, x, w.T))
+            nbytes = N * K * bpw + 2 * M * K + 2 * M * N
+            rows.append((name, M, us, cublas, nbytes, 2 * M * N * K, cfg))
+
+
+def bench_moe(args, rows):
+    for name, E, inter in MOE:
+        if args.layer not in (None, name):
+            continue
+        w1q, s1 = random_blocks((E, inter), 1024, "iq2_xxs")
+        w2q, s2 = random_blocks((E, 1024), inter, "iq2_xxs")
+        lut = t.iq2_lut(w1q.device)
+        w1 = torch.stack(
+            [t.dequantize_blocks(w1q[e], s1[e], lut, "iq2_xxs") for e in range(E)]
+        )
+        w2 = torch.stack(
+            [t.dequantize_blocks(w2q[e], s2[e], lut, "iq2_xxs") for e in range(E)]
+        )
+        relu2 = MoEActivation.RELU2_NO_MUL
+        moe_config = FusedMoEConfig(
+            num_experts=E, experts_per_token=9, hidden_dim=1024,
+            intermediate_size=inter, num_local_experts=E, num_logical_experts=E,
+            moe_parallel_config=FusedMoEParallelConfig.make_no_parallel(),
+            activation=relu2, in_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda",
+            routing_method=RoutingMethodType.TopK, max_num_tokens=max(MOE_M),
+        )  # fmt: skip
+        quant_config = FusedMoEQuantConfig(
+            _a1=FusedMoEQuantDesc(),
+            _a2=FusedMoEQuantDesc(),
+            _w1=FusedMoEQuantDesc(dtype="iq2_xxs", scale=s1),
+            _w2=FusedMoEQuantDesc(dtype="iq2_xxs", scale=s2),
+        )
+        kernel = mk.FusedMoEKernel(
+            MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular(),
+            moe.ModelOptBlockTritonExperts(moe_config, quant_config, "iq2_xxs", lut),
+        )
+        default_config = moe.moe_config
+        default_gemv = moe.moe_gemv_config
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+        for M in args.m or MOE_M:
+            x = torch.randn(M, 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            topk_ids = torch.rand(M, E, generator=gen, device="cuda").topk(9).indices
+            topk_ids = topk_ids.to(torch.int32)
+            topk_weights = torch.rand(M, 9, device="cuda").softmax(-1)
+            ours = partial(
+                kernel.apply, x, w1q, w2q, topk_weights, topk_ids,
+                activation=relu2, global_num_experts=E, expert_map=None,
+                apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+            )  # fmt: skip
+            bf16 = partial(
+                fused_experts, x, w1, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids, activation=relu2
+            )
+            ref = bf16()
+            dot_cfg = default_config(M, E, 9)
+            gemv_cfg = default_gemv(M, E, 9, "iq2_xxs")
+            candidates = [(None, gemv_cfg) if gemv_cfg else (dot_cfg, None)]
+            if args.sweep:
+                candidates += [
+                    ({"BLOCK_SIZE_M": bm, "BN": bn, "BK": bk, "num_warps": wp,
+                      "num_stages": st}, None)
+                    for bm, bn, bk, wp, st in itertools.product(
+                        (16, 32, 64, 128), (32, 64, 128), (64, 128, 256), (4, 8),
+                        (1, 2, 3),
+                    )
+                ]  # fmt: skip
+                candidates += [
+                    (None, {"BN": bn, "BK": bk, "num_warps": wp, "num_stages": st})
+                    for bn, bk, wp, st in itertools.product(
+                        (8, 16, 32, 64), (64, 128, 256), (1, 2, 4, 8), (1, 2)
+                    )
+                ]  # fmt: skip
+            timed = []
+            fallback = default_config(M, E, 9)
+            for dot_c, gemv_c in candidates:
+                moe.moe_config = lambda *_, c=dot_c or fallback: c
+                moe.moe_gemv_config = lambda *_, c=gemv_c: c
+                if (us := try_time(ours, ref)) is not None:
+                    timed.append((us, gemv_c or {**dot_c, "gemv": False}))
+            moe.moe_config = default_config
+            moe.moe_gemv_config = default_gemv
+            active = topk_ids.unique().numel()
+            nbytes = active * 2 * inter * 1024 * 66 / 256 + 4 * M * 1024
+            flops = 2 * M * 9 * 2 * inter * 1024
+            us, cfg = min(timed, key=lambda r: r[0])
+            rows.append((name, M, us, bench_us(bf16), nbytes, flops, cfg))
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--layer", help="one row name, e.g. shared_up")
+    parser.add_argument("--m", type=int, nargs="*", help="token counts")
+    parser.add_argument("--sweep", action="store_true", help="search tile configs")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    torch.set_default_device("cuda")
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    init_workspace_manager(torch.device("cuda"))
+    props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties()
+
+    src = torch.empty(1 << 30, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    copy_gbps = 2 * src.numel() / (bench_us(partial(torch.clone, src)) * 1e3)
+    del src
+    print(f"{props.name}, copy bandwidth {copy_gbps:.0f} GB/s")
+    print("layer M ours_us baseline_us ratio GB/s TFLOP/s config")
+
+    rows = []
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+        bench_dense(args, props, rows)
+        bench_moe(args, rows)
+    for name, M, us, base, nbytes, flops, cfg in rows:
+        print(
+            f"{name} {M} {us:.1f} {base:.1f} {us / base:.2f} "
+            f"{nbytes / us / 1e3:.0f} {flops / us / 1e6:.1f} {cfg}"
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

 Dense, embedding, and expert matrices remain packed. Their execution uses BF16
 activations without activation quantization. Prepare the kernels and workspaces
 before CUDA graph capture.
+
+## Other NVIDIA GPUs (Triton kernels)
+
+On NVIDIA SM75 and newer GPUs without b12x, such as T4, A100, L4, H100 and
+H200, IQ2_XXS and Q8_0 ModelOpt block weights run through Triton kernels
+instead: dense layers, routed experts, and Q8_0 embeddings. The weights stay
+packed, so memory use matches the checkpoint. The startup log shows
+`Using Triton kernels for ModelOpt IQ2_XXS ...` for each codec and layer kind.
+
+- IQ2_XS still requires b12x.
+- The Triton kernels run with BF16 or FP16 activations. b12x requires BF16, so
+  `--dtype half` uses Triton on every GPU. Turing (SM75) has no BF16 support
+  and runs FP16 only.
+- Force the Triton path with `--linear-backend triton --moe-backend triton`.
+  This also works on SM120 and SM121.
+- Routed experts support tensor parallelism only, as with b12x.
+- ROCm is not supported.
+
+With spare GPU memory and a BF16 model, cache the BF16 weights used by the
+Triton IQ2_XXS dense path:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> --kernel-config '{"modelopt_iq2_dense_cache": true}'
+```
+
+This avoids repeated dequantization for calls that already use BF16 matrix
+multiplication. Small-token GEMV and routed experts retain their packed path;
+the cache does not change their rounding or quantize activations. It adds two
+bytes per cached weight, about 3.28 GiB for Bolt's shared dense experts, within
+the `--gpu-memory-utilization` budget. Q8_0, other formats, and b12x are
+unaffected. The option is disabled by default.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Triton ModelOpt IQ2_XXS / Q8_0 kernels against a pure-torch GGML reference."""
+
+import hashlib
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from tests.kernels.moe.utils import make_dummy_moe_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import modular_kernel as mk
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
+    FusedMoEQuantConfig,
+    FusedMoEQuantDesc,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts import (
+    modelopt_block_triton_moe as moe_mod,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.modelopt_block_triton_moe import (
+    ModelOptBlockTritonExperts,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize import (
+    MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.modelopt_block_quant_triton import (
+    _IQ2XXS_GRID,
+    _linear_config,
+    dequant_min_m,
+    dequantize_blocks,
+    iq2_lut,
+    launch_linear,
+    repack_blocks,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.has_device_capability(80)),
+    reason="needs NVIDIA SM80+",
+)
+
+BLOCK = {"iq2_xxs": (256, 66), "q8_0": (32, 34)}
+# One K per codec: 4096 = 16 IQ2_XXS blocks; 1056 = 33 Q8_0 blocks (odd K / 32).
+K_FOR = {"iq2_xxs": 4096, "q8_0": 1056}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _seed():
+    set_random_seed(0)
+
+
+def ref_decode(raw: torch.Tensor, codec: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """GGML reference: [..., NB, block_bytes] uint8 -> [..., NB * block_size] fp32."""
+    lead = raw.shape[:-2]
+    blocks = raw.reshape(-1, raw.shape[-1])
+    d = blocks[:, :2].contiguous().view(torch.float16).float()
+    if codec == "q8_0":
+        q = blocks[:, 2:].contiguous().view(torch.int8).float()
+        return (d * q).reshape(*lead, -1)
+    dev = raw.device
+    grid = torch.tensor(_IQ2XXS_GRID, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    grid = ((grid[:, None] >> (8 * torch.arange(8, device=dev))) & 0xFF).float()
+    words = blocks[:, 2:].contiguous().view(torch.int32).reshape(-1, 8, 2)
+    idx, aux = words[..., 0], words[..., 1]
+    scale = d * (0.5 + ((aux >> 28) & 0xF).float()) * 0.25
+    g = torch.arange(4, device=dev)
+    gidx = (idx[..., None] >> (8 * g)) & 0xFF
+    sidx = (aux[..., None] >> (7 * g)) & 0x7F
+    parity = sidx ^ (sidx >> 4)
+    parity = parity ^ (parity >> 2)
+    parity = parity ^ (parity >> 1)
+    signs = sidx | ((parity & 1) << 7)
+    neg = (signs[..., None] >> torch.arange(8, device=dev)) & 1
+    vals = grid[gidx.long()] * (1 - 2 * neg).float()
+    return (vals * scale[..., None, None]).reshape(*lead, -1)
+
+
+def make_raw(lead, k, codec, seed, extreme=False):
+    """Random ggml blocks with finite scales; `extreme` adds 0, -d, 3e-6, 60000."""
+    size, nbytes = BLOCK[codec]
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    shape = (*lead, k // size)
+    raw = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (*shape, nbytes), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=gen
+    )
+    d = (torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 2e-3).half()
+    if extreme:
+        d.view(-1)[0::7] = 0.0
+        d.view(-1)[1::11] = -d.view(-1)[1::11].abs()
+        d.view(-1)[2::13] = 3e-6
+        d.view(-1)[3::17] = 60000.0
+    raw[..., :2] = d.unsqueeze(-1).view(torch.uint8)
+    return raw
+
+
+def linear(x, raw, codec):
+    qweight, scales = repack_blocks(raw, codec)
+    lut = iq2_lut(raw.device) if codec == "iq2_xxs" else None
+    return torch.ops.vllm.modelopt_block_linear(x, qweight, scales, lut, codec)
+
+
+def assert_close_to_cublas(out, x, w):
+    """Our error vs the exact product must be within 1.5x of cuBLAS's in x.dtype."""
+    want = x.double() @ w.double().T
+    cublas = (x @ w.to(x.dtype).T).double()
+    ours = (out.double() - want).abs().max()
+    assert ours <= 1.5 * (cublas - want).abs().max() + 1e-6, ours
+
+
+def test_iq2_grid_matches_ggml():
+    grid = torch.tensor(_IQ2XXS_GRID, dtype=torch.int64)
+    assert (
+        hashlib.sha256(grid.numpy().tobytes()).hexdigest()
+        == "05826b5d3e472a3a78f196be62ac78acf81df0f909626e12ab9fa2a5d490dd54"
+    )
+    quants = pytest.importorskip("gguf.quants")
+    quants.IQ2_XXS.init_grid()
+    expected = torch.from_numpy(quants.IQ2_XXS.grid.reshape(256, 8).astype("int64"))
+    assert torch.equal((grid[:, None] >> (8 * torch.arange(8))) & 0xFF, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("codec", ["iq2_xxs", "q8_0"])
+def test_decode_bit_exact(codec):
+    """Both decodes, table gather (dequant) and 2-bit codes (GEMM), are exact."""
+    K = K_FOR[codec]
+    raw = make_raw((264,), K, codec, seed=1, extreme=True)
+    qweight, scales = repack_blocks(raw, codec)
+    lut = iq2_lut(raw.device) if codec == "iq2_xxs" else None
+    want = ref_decode(raw, codec).bfloat16()
+    assert torch.equal(dequantize_blocks(qweight, scales, lut, codec), want)
+    eye = torch.eye(K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gemm = {"BM": 64, "BN": 64, "BK": 32, "SPLIT": 1, "num_warps": 4, "num_stages": 2}
+    assert torch.equal(launch_linear(eye, qweight, scales, lut, codec, gemm).T, want)
+

+def ref_moe(x, w1, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids, activation, dtype):
+    """Unfused MoE with every intermediate rounded to `dtype`."""
+    x, out = x.to(dtype), torch.zeros(x.shape, dtype=torch.float64, device=x.device)
+    for e in range(w1.shape[0]):
+        token, slot = (topk_ids == e).nonzero(as_tuple=True)
+        h = x[token] @ w1[e].to(dtype).T
+        if activation == MoEActivation.SILU:
+            gate, up = h.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+            h = F.silu(gate) * up
+        else:
+            h = F.relu(h).square()
+        y = (h @ w2[e].to(dtype).T) * topk_weights[token, slot, None].to(dtype)
+        out.index_add_(0, token, y.double())
+    return out
+

+def assert_moe_close_to_unfused(out, x, w1, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids, activation):
+    """Our error vs the exact MoE must be within 2x of an unfused MoE's in x.dtype.
+
+    Over random inputs the ratio has a median of ~0.9 and a tail to ~1.6; a
+    routing or weighting bug is orders of magnitude off.
+
+    Plus one ulp of the output scale: the fused contract keeps c1/c2 in the
+    model dtype, so anything under a ulp of the largest output cannot show up in
+    the result. Real Bolt expert weights need this slack at decode sizes (2-4x
+    the bare 2x bar at M=4) while matching a torch simulation of the same bf16
+    buffer chain exactly, so the slack is the buffers, not the kernels.
+    """
+    want = ref_moe(x, w1, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids, activation, torch.float64)
+    unfused = ref_moe(x, w1, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids, activation, x.dtype)
+    ours = (out.double() - want).abs().max()
+    ulp = want.abs().max().double() * torch.finfo(x.dtype).eps / 2
+    assert ours <= 2 * (unfused - want).abs().max() + ulp + 1e-6, ours
+

+def repack_blocks(raw: torch.Tensor, codec: str) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Split ggml blocks into an aligned payload and fp16 block scales.
+
+    Args:
+        raw: uint8 [..., NB, 66] (IQ2_XXS) or [..., NB, 34] (Q8_0).
+        codec: "iq2_xxs" or "q8_0".
+
+    Returns:
+        qweight: int32 [..., NB * 16] (IQ2_XXS) or int8 [..., NB * 32] (Q8_0).
+        scales: fp16 [..., NB].
+
+    """
+    scales = raw[..., :2].contiguous().view(torch.float16).squeeze(-1)
+    payload = raw[..., 2:].contiguous().flatten(-2)
+    return payload.view(torch.int32 if codec == "iq2_xxs" else torch.int8), scales
+

+@functools.cache
+def iq2_lut(device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """int32 [256 * 8 + 256]: the grid's fp32 magnitudes (8, 25 or 43) as bits,
+    then each entry's 8 magnitudes as 2-bit codes. Build at load time.
+    """
+    grid = torch.tensor(_IQ2XXS_GRID, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    shifts = torch.arange(8, device=device)
+    mags = (grid[:, None] >> (8 * shifts)) & 0xFF
+    codes = ((mags > 8).long() + (mags > 25).long()) << (2 * shifts)
+    return torch.cat([mags.float().view(torch.int32).flatten(), codes.sum(-1).int()])

+def _decode_tile(
+    qw_ptr,
+    sc_ptr,
+    lut_ptr,
+    offs_n,
+    n_mask,
+    k0,
+    stride_qn,
+    stride_sn,
+    CODEC: tl.constexpr,
+    GATHER: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Weights [offs_n, k0:k0+BK] as an fp32 [BN, BK] tile; BK % 32 == 0.
+
+    GATHER loads IQ2 magnitudes from the fp32 table, which vectorizes in the
+    blocked layouts of the GEMV and dequant kernels. In `tl.dot` operand layouts
+    it doesn't, and unpacking 2-bit codes is faster.
+    """
+    R: tl.constexpr = BK // 32
+    rr = k0 // 32 + tl.arange(0, R)
+    row = offs_n.to(tl.int64)[:, None]
+    if CODEC == 1:
+        # Per record: scale. Per group of 8: grid index and sign mask.
+        d = tl.load(
+            sc_ptr + row * stride_sn + (rr // 8)[None, :],
+            mask=n_mask[:, None],
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        idx = tl.load(
+            qw_ptr + row * stride_qn + (2 * rr)[None, :], mask=n_mask[:, None], other=0
+        )
+        aux = tl.load(
+            qw_ptr + row * stride_qn + (2 * rr + 1)[None, :],
+            mask=n_mask[:, None],
+            other=0,
+        )
+        rs = d * (0.5 + ((aux >> 28) & 15).to(tl.float32)) * 0.25
+        g = tl.arange(0, 4)[None, None, :]
+        gidx = (idx[:, :, None] >> (8 * g)) & 255
+        s = (aux[:, :, None] >> (7 * g)) & 127
+        p = s ^ (s >> 4)
+        p = p ^ (p >> 2)
+        p = p ^ (p >> 1)
+        smask = s | ((p & 1) << 7)
+        j = tl.arange(0, 8)[None, None, None, :]
+        if GATHER:
+            mag = tl.load(lut_ptr + gidx[:, :, :, None] * 8 + j)
+            mag = mag.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+        else:
+            codes = tl.load(lut_ptr + 2048 + gidx)
+            c = (codes[:, :, :, None] >> (2 * j)) & 3
+            mag = tl.where(c == 0, 8.0, tl.where(c == 1, 25.0, 43.0))
+        neg = (smask[:, :, :, None] >> j) & 1
+        w = tl.where(neg != 0, -mag, mag) * rs[:, :, None, None]
+        w = tl.reshape(w, (BN, BK))
+    else:
+        d = tl.load(
+            sc_ptr + row * stride_sn + rr[None, :], mask=n_mask[:, None], other=0.0
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        q = tl.load(
+            qw_ptr + row * stride_qn + (k0 + tl.arange(0, BK))[None, :],
+            mask=n_mask[:, None],
+            other=0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        w = tl.reshape(tl.reshape(q, (BN, R, 32)) * d[:, :, None], (BN, BK))
+    return w

+    topk_weights_ptr,
+    sorted_token_ids_ptr,
+    expert_ids_ptr,
+    N,
+    K,
+    num_valid_tokens,
+    stride_am,
+    stride_qe,
+    stride_qn,
+    stride_se,
+    stride_sn,
+    stride_cm,
+    top_k: tl.constexpr,
+    MUL_ROUTED_WEIGHT: tl.constexpr,
+    CODEC: tl.constexpr,
+    DIRECT_ROUTING: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+    APPLY_RELU2: tl.constexpr = False,
+):
+    """One routed row per program: c[slot] = a[slot // top_k] @ W[e]^T.
+
+    For decode, when there are fewer routed rows than experts: no tensor cores,
+    so no rows are decoded that nobody asked for, and the LUT gather decode
+    beats the 2-bit codes used by `_moe_gemm_kernel`'s `tl.dot` layout.
+    """
+    slot = tl.program_id(0)
+    if DIRECT_ROUTING:
+        offs_token = slot.to(tl.int64)
+    else:
+        offs_token = tl.load(sorted_token_ids_ptr + slot).to(tl.int64)
+    valid = offs_token < num_valid_tokens
+    # A padding slot reads row 0 and an expert that exists; only its store is off.
+    row = tl.where(valid, offs_token, 0) // top_k
+    e = tl.load(expert_ids_ptr + slot).to(tl.int64)
+    offs_n = tl.program_id(1) * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    n_mask = offs_n < N
+    a_row = a_ptr + row * stride_am
+    qw_ptr += e * stride_qe
+    sc_ptr += e * stride_se
+    acc = tl.zeros((BN,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    for k0 in range(0, K, BK):
+        w = _decode_tile(
+            qw_ptr, sc_ptr, lut_ptr, offs_n, n_mask, k0, stride_qn, stride_sn,
+            CODEC, True, BN, BK,
+        )  # fmt: skip
+        x = tl.load(a_row + k0 + tl.arange(0, BK)).to(tl.float32)
+        acc += tl.sum(w * x[None, :], axis=1)
+    if MUL_ROUTED_WEIGHT:
+        weight = tl.load(topk_weights_ptr + offs_token, mask=valid, other=0.0)
+        acc *= weight.to(tl.float32)
+    if APPLY_RELU2:
+        # Preserve the intermediate stored by the unfused first GEMM.
+        value = tl.maximum(acc.to(c_ptr.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32), 0.0)
+        acc = value * value
+    tl.store(
+        c_ptr + offs_token * stride_cm + offs_n,
+        acc.to(c_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=valid & n_mask,
+    )
+

+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["total", "split"])
+def _splitk_reduce_kernel(p_ptr, out_ptr, total, split, BN: tl.constexpr):
+    """Sum the split-K partials: p [split, total] fp32 -> [total] in out's dtype."""
+    offs = tl.program_id(0) * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    mask = offs < total
+    acc = tl.load(p_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    for s in range(1, split):
+        acc += tl.load(p_ptr + s * total + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offs, acc.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _q8_embedding_kernel(
+    ids_ptr, qw_ptr, sc_ptr, out_ptr, H, stride_qn, stride_sn, stride_om,
+    BH: tl.constexpr,
+):  # fmt: skip
+    t = tl.program_id(0)
+    offs = tl.program_id(1) * BH + tl.arange(0, BH)
+    mask = offs < H
+    row = tl.load(ids_ptr + t).to(tl.int64)
+    q = tl.load(qw_ptr + row * stride_qn + offs, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+    d = tl.load(sc_ptr + row * stride_sn + offs // 32, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + t.to(tl.int64) * stride_om + offs,
+        (q * d).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=mask,
+    )
+
+
+def _linear_config(
+    M: int, N: int, K: int, codec: str, num_sms: int, smem: int, major: int
+) -> dict[str, int]:
+    if (
+        major == 9
+        and codec == "q8_0"
+        and M == 1
+        and (N, K) in ((256, 4096), (1024, 4096), (4096, 4096), (4096, 1024))
+    ):
+        # Hopper decode: wider K tiles avoid a separate split-K reduction.
+        return {
+            "BM": 1,
+            "BN": 4,
+            "BK": min(K, 1024) if N == 4096 else K,
+            "SPLIT": 1,
+            "num_warps": 4,
+            "num_stages": 1,
+        }
+    if M == 1 or (codec == "iq2_xxs" and M <= 4):
+        # GEMV; for IQ2 it beats tl.dot up to 4 rows.
+        bm = triton.next_power_of_2(M)
+        bn, bk, warps = (8, 256, 1) if codec == "iq2_xxs" else (32, 256, 4)
+    elif M <= 16:
+        bm, bn, bk, warps = 16, 64, 128, 4
+    elif M <= 64:
+        bm, bn, bk, warps = 32 if M <= 32 else 64, 64, 128, 4
+    else:
+        bm, bn, bk, warps = 128 if smem >= 160 * 1024 else 64, 128, 64, 8
+    stages = 2
+    if major < 8 and bm >= 16:
+        # Turing has no tensor-core tl.dot; these FMA tiles don't spill on SM75.
+        bm, bn, bk, warps, stages = min(bm, 64), 64, 32, 8, 1
+    bk = next(b for b in (256, 128, 64, 32) if b <= bk and K % b == 0)
+    # Deterministic split-K (fp32 partials) until the grid covers the GPU a few
+    # times. GEMV tiles are decode-bound, so give them many more CTAs; IQ2 spends
+    # the extra parallelism on unpacking the grid.
+    tiles = triton.cdiv(M, bm) * triton.cdiv(N, bn)
+    target = (8 if codec == "q8_0" else 32) * num_sms if M <= 4 else 2 * num_sms
+    k_steps = K // bk
+    split = 1
+    while split < 16 and tiles * split < target and k_steps % (2 * split) == 0:
+        split *= 2
+    if split == 1:
+        # No power of two divides the K step count, so the grid stays narrow and
+        # stalls on decode latency: shared_down has 5376 / 256 = 21 steps. Take
+        # any divisor instead, which is still a deterministic fp32 reduction.
+        for d in range(min(16, k_steps), 1, -1):
+            if k_steps % d == 0 and tiles * d < 2 * target:
+                split = d
+                break
+    return {
+        "BM": bm,
+        "BN": bn,
+        "BK": bk,
+        "SPLIT": split,
+        "num_warps": warps,
+        "num_stages": stages,
+    }
+
+
+def launch_linear(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    lut: torch.Tensor | None,
+    codec: str,
+    cfg: dict[str, int],
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`modelopt_block_linear` with an explicit `_linear_config`-style config."""
+    M, K = x.shape
+    N = qweight.shape[0]
+    split = cfg["SPLIT"]
+    out = (
+        x.new_empty((M, N))
+        if split == 1
+        else torch.empty((split, M, N), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    )
+    launch = {"num_warps": cfg["num_warps"], "num_stages": cfg["num_stages"]}
+    if cfg["BM"] < 16:  # tl.dot needs BM >= 16
+        assert cfg["BM"] >= M
+        _gemv_kernel[(triton.cdiv(N, cfg["BN"]), split)](
+            x, qweight, scales, lut, out, M, N, K // split, x.stride(0),
+            qweight.stride(0), scales.stride(0), CODEC=_CODEC_ID[codec],
+            BM=cfg["BM"], BN=cfg["BN"], BK=cfg["BK"], **launch,
+        )  # fmt: skip
+    else:
+        grid = (triton.cdiv(M, cfg["BM"]) * triton.cdiv(N, cfg["BN"]), split)
+        _gemm_kernel[grid](
+            x, qweight, scales, lut, out, M, N, K // split, x.stride(0),
+            qweight.stride(0), scales.stride(0), CODEC=_CODEC_ID[codec],
+            BM=cfg["BM"], BN=cfg["BN"], BK=cfg["BK"], **launch,
+        )  # fmt: skip
+    if split == 1:
+        return out
+    y = x.new_empty((M, N))
+    total = M * N
+    _splitk_reduce_kernel[(triton.cdiv(total, 1024),)](
+        out, y, total, split, BN=1024, num_warps=4
+    )  # fmt: skip
+    return y
+
+
+def dequantize_blocks(
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    lut: torch.Tensor | None,
+    codec: str,
+    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[N, K] in `dtype` from 2-D `repack_blocks` output."""
+    N, nb = scales.shape
+    K = nb * (256 if codec == "iq2_xxs" else 32)
+    out = torch.empty((N, K), dtype=dtype, device=qweight.device)
+    bk = next(b for b in (256, 128, 64, 32) if K % b == 0)
+    bn, warps = (8, 1) if codec == "iq2_xxs" else (32, 4)
+    _dequant_kernel[(triton.cdiv(N, bn), K // bk)](
+        qweight, scales, lut, out, N, K, qweight.stride(0), scales.stride(0),
+        CODEC=_CODEC_ID[codec], BN=bn, BK=bk, num_warps=warps,
+    )  # fmt: skip
+    return out
+
+
+# From this many tokens, dequantize once and use cuBLAS, as AWQ does: the fused
+# GEMM decodes W once per M tile. Capping the copy at 128 MiB keeps lm_head on
+# the fused GEMM. The copy is a write and a read of 2 bytes per weight, so the
+# crossover tracks memory bandwidth. Values are (HBM, GDDR). On GDDR the fused
+# IQ2_XXS GEMM doubles in cost past one 64-row M tile, hence 65.
+DEQUANT_MIN_M = {"iq2_xxs": (8, 65), "q8_0": (64, 256)}
+DEQUANT_MAX_NUMEL = 1 << 26
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _is_hbm(device: int) -> bool:
+    # Bus width as the bandwidth class: HBM is at least 1024 bits wide.
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).memory_bus_width >= 1024
+
+
+def dequant_min_m(codec: str, device: int) -> int:
+    """Token count from which `modelopt_block_linear` dequantizes for cuBLAS."""
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).major < 8:
+        # Turing's fused GEMM runs on FMA while cuBLAS keeps tensor cores.
+        # 32 is a roofline estimate for T4.
+        return 32
+    return DEQUANT_MIN_M[codec][not _is_hbm(device)]
+
+
+def _modelopt_block_linear(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    qweight: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+    lut: torch.Tensor | None,
+    codec: str,
+    weight_bf16: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Packed block GEMM; picks the kernel from M inside the op.
+
+    Args:
+        x: bf16 or fp16 [M, K].
+        qweight: int32 [N, K / 16] (IQ2_XXS) or int8 [N, K] (Q8_0).
+        scales: fp16 [N, K / block_size].
+        lut: `iq2_lut` for IQ2_XXS, None for Q8_0.
+        codec: "iq2_xxs" or "q8_0".
+        weight_bf16: Optional cached dequantized weights for the BF16 GEMM path.
+
+    Returns:
+        [M, N] in x's dtype.
+
+    """
+    M, K = x.shape
+    if M == 0:
+        return x.new_empty((0, qweight.shape[0]))
+    if (
+        dequant_min_m(codec, x.device.index) <= M
+        and qweight.shape[0] * K <= DEQUANT_MAX_NUMEL
+    ):
+        weight = (
+            weight_bf16
+            if weight_bf16 is not None
+            else dequantize_blocks(qweight, scales, lut, codec, x.dtype)
+        )
+        return x @ weight.T
+    if x.stride(1) != 1:
+        x = x.contiguous()
+    props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(x.device)
+    cfg = _linear_config(
+        M,
+        qweight.shape[0],
+        K,
+        codec,
+        props.multi_processor_count,
+        props.shared_memory_per_block_optin,
+        props.major,
+    )
+    return launch_linear(x, qweight, scales, lut, codec, cfg)
+

+def _modelopt_block_embedding_fake(

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Warm the ModelOpt block Triton kernels used by a loaded model.
+
+The dense dispatch picks a tile from the token count inside the custom op, so a
+prefill chunk of any size can reach a config that the dummy runs never touched.
+Compile every distinct config once, before CUDA graph capture, so inference does
+not JIT.
+"""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker import Worker
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def _warmup_token_counts(worker: "Worker") -> int:
+    scheduler = worker.scheduler_config
+    compilation = worker.vllm_config.compilation_config
+    sizes = [
+        1,
+        scheduler.max_num_batched_tokens,
+        scheduler.max_num_seqs,
+        *(compilation.cudagraph_capture_sizes or []),
+        *(s for s in (compilation.compile_sizes or []) if isinstance(s, int)),
+    ]
+    return max(int(size) for size in sizes)
+
+
+def _triton_layers(model: torch.nn.Module):
+    for module in model.modules():
+        method = getattr(module, "quant_method", None)
+        if method is not None and getattr(method, "use_triton", False):
+            yield module, method
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def modelopt_block_triton_warmup(worker: "Worker") -> None:
+    """Compile every ModelOpt block config reachable at serving token counts."""
+    if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+        return
+
+    model = worker.get_model()
+    layers = list(_triton_layers(model))
+    if not layers:
+        return
+
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_align_block_size import (
+        moe_align_block_size,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import (
+        modelopt_block_quant_triton as kernels,
+    )
+
+    max_tokens = _warmup_token_counts(worker)
+    props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(worker.device)
+    dtype = worker.vllm_config.model_config.dtype
+    num_sms = props.multi_processor_count
+    smem = props.shared_memory_per_block_optin
+
+    warmed = 0
+    seen_linear: set[tuple] = set()
+    seen_dequant: set[tuple] = set()
+    seen_moe: set[tuple] = set()
+
+    for module, method in layers:
+        codec = method.codec
+        if hasattr(module, "w13_weight"):
+            _warm_moe(
+                module,
+                method,
+                kernels,
+                moe_align_block_size,
+                max_tokens,
+                seen_moe,
+                dtype,
+            )
+            warmed += 1
+            continue
+
+        device = module.weight.device
+        if getattr(method, "is_embedding", False):
+            for id_dtype in (torch.int64, torch.int32):
+                ids = torch.zeros(1, dtype=id_dtype, device=device)
+                torch.ops.vllm.modelopt_block_embedding(
+                    ids, module.weight, module.weight_scale, dtype
+                )
+            warmed += 1
+            continue
+
+        qweight = module.weight
+        n = qweight.shape[0]
+        k = module.weight_scale.shape[1] * method.block_size
+        fused_configs: dict[tuple, int] = {}
+        min_m = kernels.dequant_min_m(codec, device.index)
+        for m in range(1, max_tokens + 1):
+            if m >= min_m and n * k <= kernels.DEQUANT_MAX_NUMEL:
+                key: tuple = (codec, n, k)
+                if key not in seen_dequant:
+                    seen_dequant.add(key)
+                    x = torch.zeros((min_m, k), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+                    torch.ops.vllm.modelopt_block_linear(
+                        x,
+                        qweight,
+                        module.weight_scale,
+                        getattr(module, "iq2_lut", None),
+                        codec,
+                        getattr(module, "weight_bf16", None),
+                    )
+                    warmed += 1
+                continue
+            cfg = kernels._linear_config(m, n, k, codec, num_sms, smem, props.major)
+            key = (codec, n, k, tuple(sorted(cfg.items())))
+            if key not in seen_linear:
+                seen_linear.add(key)
+                fused_configs[key] = m
+        for key, m in fused_configs.items():
+            x = torch.zeros((m, k), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+            torch.ops.vllm.modelopt_block_linear(
+                x,
+                qweight,
+                module.weight_scale,
+                getattr(module, "iq2_lut", None),
+                codec,
+                getattr(module, "weight_bf16", None),
+            )
+            warmed += 1
+
+    if warmed:
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        logger.info("Warmed %d ModelOpt block Triton configs.", warmed)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def _warm_moe(
+    module: torch.nn.Module,
+    method,
+    kernels,
+    moe_align_block_size,
+    max_tokens: int,
+    seen: set[tuple],
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> None:
+    codec = method.codec
+    device = module.w13_weight.device
+    num_experts = module.w13_weight.shape[0]
+    top_k = module.top_k
+    warm_k = module.w2_weight.shape[1]
+    n1 = module.w13_weight.shape[1]
+    n2 = module.w2_weight.shape[1]
+    k2 = module.w2_weight_scale.shape[2] * method.block_size
+    mul_routed_weight = not module.apply_router_weight_on_input
+    lut = kernels.iq2_lut(device) if codec == "iq2_xxs" else None
+
+    configs: dict[tuple, tuple[dict[str, int], bool]] = {}
+    for m in range(1, max_tokens + 1):
+        gemv = kernels.moe_gemv_config(m, num_experts, top_k, codec)
+        cfg = gemv or kernels.moe_config(m, num_experts, top_k)
+        key = (
+            codec,
+            n1,
+            warm_k,
+            n2,
+            k2,
+            top_k,
+            mul_routed_weight,
+            gemv is not None,
+            module.expert_map is None,
+            module.activation,
+            tuple(sorted(cfg.items())),
+        )
+        if key in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(key)
+        configs[key] = (cfg, gemv is not None)
+
+    for key, (cfg, gemv) in configs.items():
+        launch = (
+            kernels.invoke_block_moe_gemv_kernel
+            if gemv
+            else kernels.invoke_block_moe_kernel
+        )
+        # One aligned block per routed row on the GEMV path; the token count there
+        # only sizes the dummy routing, the kernel takes no tile in M.
+        bm = 1 if gemv else cfg["BLOCK_SIZE_M"]
+        rows = 2 if gemv else bm
+        topk_ids = torch.randint(
+            0, num_experts, (rows, top_k), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        topk_weights = torch.rand((rows, top_k), dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        routing = (
+            (None, topk_ids, None)
+            if gemv and module.expert_map is None
+            else moe_align_block_size(topk_ids, bm, num_experts, module.expert_map)
+        )
+        a1 = torch.zeros((rows, warm_k), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        c1 = torch.empty((rows, top_k, n1), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        launch(
+            a1,
+            module.w13_weight,
+            module.w13_weight_scale,
+            lut,
+            c1,
+            None,
+            *routing,
+            False,
+            top_k,
+            cfg,
+            codec,
+            # MoEActivation is a plain Enum: compare its value, not the member.
+            **(
+                {"apply_relu2": module.activation.value == "relu2_no_mul"}
+                if gemv
+                else {}
+            ),
+        )
+        a2 = torch.empty((rows * top_k, k2), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        c2 = torch.empty((rows, top_k, n2), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        launch(
+            a2,
+            module.w2_weight,
+            module.w2_weight_scale,
+            lut,
+            c2,
+            topk_weights,
+            *routing,
+            mul_routed_weight,
+            1,
+            cfg,
+            codec,
+        )
+        del topk_ids, topk_weights, routing, a1, c1, a2, c2
